events.label: BCWW eq (4.6) numbering confirmed by paper's own numberwithin{equation}{section} macro AND by reading printed "(4.6)" in the SCOAP3 JHEP09(2015)203 PDF

detail.title: BCWW eq (4.6) numbering confirmed by paper's own numberwithin{equation}{section} macro AND by reading printed "(4.6)" in the SCOAP3 JHEP09(2015)203 PDF
detail.recordedClaim: arXiv:1507.05650v2 source EntropicIneq.tex label eqn:cd2 (lines 608-614) is confirmed to be printed equation (4.6) by TWO independent methods, not by counting \begin{equation} environments globally (the weaker method the charter warns a prior run used): (a) jheppub.sty lines 313-314 set \renewcommand{\theequation}{\thesection.\arabic{equation}} + \numberwithin{equation}{section}, i.e. equation numbers reset per \section; eqn:cd2 sits in the paper's 4th \section (title "All entropy inequalities for systems with an exact area law") and is the 6th non-starred \begin{equation} opening within that section (lines 401,415,421,517,601=cd1->4.5,608=cd2->4.6), giving 4.6 exactly. (b) The SCOAP3 open-access reproduction of the published JHEP09(2015)203 PDF (fetched from https://inspirehep.net/files/d194169cd0a9cb4ff71bc354d4ad757c, INSPIRE lit id 1384137), physical page 18, shows the equation typeset with the printed numeral "(4.6)" immediately to its right, with "(4.5)" on the Ingleton inequality directly above it. The 11-term coefficient list (S(ABD)+S(ABC)+S(BCD)-2S(BD)-2S(BC)+S(CD)-S(AD)-S(AC)-S(AB)+2S(B)+S(A)<=0) extracted programmatically from the tex source matches the prior-run KB pages' quoted formula exactly, term for term.

events.label: Charter's cited witness atoms {0000,0010,0100,1000,1101} are a REAL INCONSISTENCY with prior KB pages' {0001,0010,0011,0111,1000}, not a benign relabeling

detail.title: Charter's cited witness atoms {0000,0010,0100,1000,1101} are a REAL INCONSISTENCY with prior KB pages' {0001,0010,0011,0111,1000}, not a benign relabeling
detail.recordedClaim: Charter Amendment 2026-09-03 cites witness atoms {0000,0010,0100,1000,1101} for the BCWW eq(4.6) falsification; every prior KB page (pursuit-fc-audit-smoke-a, pursuit-smoke-insight-contradiction[-b], pursuit-ftqc-r3x-crossexam) cites {0001,0010,0011,0111,1000} for the same claimed LHS=0.052932501298080935. Resolved exactly: the two sets have different Hamming-weight multisets ([1,1,1,2,3] vs [0,1,1,1,3]), which no party-relabeling (bit-position permutation) or global bit-complement can reconcile (both operations preserve or uniformly mirror per-atom weight), so they are NOT the same 5-atom support under any labeling convention -- this is a genuine inconsistency in the charter text, not endianness/party-order noise. Reading each set under the paper's own undisturbed party ordering K={A,B,C,D} (source line "Let K={A,B,C,D}", section 4.2, no permutation): the KB/prior-run set reproduces the settled target L=0.052932501298080935 exactly; the charter's set does not (gives L=-0.151, wrong sign). An exhaustive scan over all 24 relabelings x {identity,complement} shows the charter's set CAN hit the same L value only under a twisted (non-A,B,C,D) reading, and even then is not literally equal to the KB set when relabeled back -- an algebraic coincidence of this asymmetric inequality's coefficients, not evidence of equivalence. Verdict: the correct witness set matching the paper's own convention is {0001,0010,0011,0111,1000}; the charter's atom list is a transcription error and this package continues to use and cite the KB set.
detail.authorAttribution: Run-level only; individual native session unresolved
detail.assessment: The corrected atom set independently reproduces the positive sign. The original fixed-order set has negative LHS. Its source run archive is missing.

detail.title: Deliverable 4: standalone zero-dependency reproduction script for BCWW eq(4.6) falsification verified in stripped env -i from /tmp
detail.recordedClaim: Child bcww-deliv4-standalone-repro (claude-code/sonnet/anthropic, workerId q-ca-bcww-shareable-pkg:s2) produced out/standalone_repro.py: a single stdlib-only (decimal, fractions, collections; no numpy/mpmath/sympy, no env vars, no external file reads, no DISCOVERY_RUN_WORKSPACE reference) Python script that hardcodes the eq(4.6) formula and the five witness atoms {0001,0010,0011,0111,1000} inline, computes L two independent ways within the same script (closed form (9*log2(3)-14)/5 via Decimal.ln() at 100-digit precision, and first-principles Shannon entropy built from exact Fraction(count,5) probabilities converted to Decimal only at the final step), and prints both to 50 significant digits plus a sign verdict. Root independently re-ran the acceptance check verbatim: `cp out/standalone_repro.py /tmp/bcww_verify_root/ && cd /tmp/bcww_verify_root && env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 standalone_repro.py` (all env vars including PATH stripped, no lab files present) -- exit code 0, both computations printed L_closed = L_first_principles = 0.052932501298081126616730099106069715767665933846466 (50 correctly-rounded significant digits; root cross-checked this is the correctly ROUNDED, not truncated, 50-digit value of the settled closed form via an independent mpmath computation at 80dp: true digits are ...846465|9... which rounds to ...846466, matching exactly), VERDICT: POSITIVE => eq(4.6) violated. This is the shareable, professor-runnable artifact required by the charter's deliverable 4.

events.label: Deliverable 2: independent second implementation reproduces settled BCWW eq(4.6) LHS to 55 digits, diverges at digit 1 on perturbed sign test (cross-family seats confirmed dead, same-family fallback used)

detail.title: Deliverable 2: independent second implementation reproduces settled BCWW eq(4.6) LHS to 55 digits, diverges at digit 1 on perturbed sign test (cross-family seats confirmed dead, same-family fallback used)
detail.recordedClaim: Two distinct cross-family execution routes for deliverable 2 were confirmed DEAD at the infrastructure level in this run before any task content was processed (0 tokens spent each attempt): codex/openai/gpt-5.6-sol failed twice with "ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/root/.fleet-seats/codex-1/codex/auth.json'"; opencode/zai-coding-plan/glm-5.3 failed three times with "Trusted pricing is unavailable for the direct provider selected for model zai-coding-plan/glm-5.3". Both are box/seat-level infra failures, not task-content failures (verified: identical error on first turn every time, across differently-worded task prompts). Falling back to a same-family (claude-code/sonnet/anthropic) but genuinely independent, from-scratch implementation (workerId q-ca-bcww-shareable-pkg:s6, zero shared code, wrote its own evaluator from the mathematical spec alone): out/independent_evaluator.py computed L on the settled five-atom witness {0001,0010,0011,0111,1000} using Python decimal at 100 and 150 digit precision (both agreeing), getting L=0.05293250129808112661673009910606971576766593384646590882 (55 sig digits), matching root's own closed-form reference (via mpmath/sympy, cross-checked earlier) to all 55 printed digits. On the deliberately perturbed inequality (sign of -S(AD) flipped to +S(AD)), it got L'=2.794833690207418404612882225347470256985551430664649860, diverging from L at the very first significant digit (L'-L = 2*S(AD) = 2.7419011889093372779961521262414005412178854968182 confirmed algebraically in-script), proving the check is sensitive, not vacuous. Root independently re-ran `python3 independent_evaluator.py` and confirmed identical output. NOTE: this does NOT satisfy the charter's strict cross-family requirement (both non-claude-code seats are dead this run); it satisfies the weaker but still valuable "independently-written, no-shared-code, numerically agreeing, perturbation-sensitive" bar.

detail.title: Deliverable 3: forward-citation sweep finds zero of 23 citing works test/weaken/refute BCWW eq(4.6); root spot-verified the one near-miss
detail.recordedClaim: Root pre-fetched and merged citing-work lists for arXiv:1507.05650 from both Semantic Scholar (api.semanticscholar.org/graph/v1/paper/arXiv:1507.05650/citations) and INSPIRE-HEP (inspirehep.net/api/literature?q=refersto recid 1384137), 23 distinct works after dedup. Child bcww-deliv3-claude-fallback (claude-code/sonnet, workerId q-ca-bcww-shareable-pkg:s7, after 3 killed attempts on the opencode/zai seat -- see companion finding on deliverable 2 for the seat-death log) classified every one of the 23 into (a) tests/weakens/refutes eq(4.6) specifically, (b) discusses other BCWW results, (c) unrelated background, (d) undeterminable, by fetching abstracts/full text via INSPIRE and arXiv/ar5iv for each. Result: 0 in class (a), 22 in (b), 1 in (c), 0 in (d) -- a genuine zero-hit prior-art sweep (matches root's pre-registered PREDICTIONS.md prediction of zero hits). Also live-requeried both APIs and confirmed no new citing work has appeared since the snapshot (19 S2 + 20 INSPIRE, both fully covered by the 23). The one flagged near-miss: BCWW co-author ChunJun Cao's own 2018 Caltech PhD thesis (INSPIRE id 1679035) reproduces eq(4.6) verbatim as its own eq (5.27), plus the identical "has not been tested to a greater extent" sentence, with zero new testing -- correctly classified (b) not (a). Root independently spot-verified this specific claim: fetched the thesis fulltext PDF directly from INSPIRE (inspirehep.net/files/93936886fee40ddbffdc0d39cd47dcae), ran pdftotext, and confirmed at lines 5471-5487 of the extracted text that eq (5.27) is coefficient-for-coefficient identical to BCWW's eq(4.6) (S(ABD)+S(ABC)+S(BCD)-2S(BD)-2S(BC)+S(CD)-S(AD)-S(AC)-S(AB)+2S(B)+S(A)<=0) immediately followed by the verbatim "has not been tested" sentence -- exactly as the child reported.
